question: Who was the founder of the Sattriya dance form of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sankardev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sankardev** (1449–1568) was a saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer from Assam.
 
• He is credited with creating **Sattriya dance**, a classical dance form of India, as part of the **Neo-Vaishnavite movement** in Assam.
 
• Sattriya dance was originally performed in **monastic institutions called Satras**, established by Sankardev to propagate the Vaishnavite philosophy.
 
• The dance form serves as a medium for storytelling and is deeply rooted in **mythological themes and devotional expressions**.
 
• Sattriya was officially recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sankardev's Neo-Vaishnavism Movement**

 
 
• Sankardev propagated the **Ekasarana Dharma**, a monotheistic religious movement emphasizing devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• He used art forms like music (Borgeet), dance (Sattriya), and drama (Ankiya Nat) to spread his teachings.
 
• The movement rejected caste discrimination and ritualistic practices, promoting equality and devotion.
 
 
 
• **Satras**
 
 
• Satras are monastic institutions established by Sankardev and his disciples in Assam to promote Vaishnavism.
 
• They function as cultural hubs for the preservation of art, literature, and religious practices.
 
• Sattriya dance evolved and thrived within these institutions.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Characteristics**
 
 
• The dance combines **expressive hand gestures (mudras), rhythmic footwork, and storytelling**.
 
• It incorporates themes from the **Bhagavata Purana and Krishna-centric mythology**.
 
• Traditionally performed by male monks (Bhakats), it is now practiced by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Sattriya Dance**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized Sattriya as a classical dance form in 2000, bringing it to a national platform.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve this cultural heritage and promote it globally.
